questions.question: Answers spanning chunk boundaries go missing from retrieval. What windowing prevents that?
options: Bigger gaps between chunks
Single chunks per document
No chunking at all
Overlapped fixed windows covering boundaries
questions.explanation: Gaps lose boundary answers. This lesson overlaps windows so evidence survives splitting.

questions.question: Which separator does chunk_recursive try before a single newline?
options: A space
A double newline
A comma
No separator; it always slices fixed widths first
questions.explanation: The default separators are ordered (double newline, newline, period-space, space), and the first present separator is used.

questions.question: When does chunk_semantic start a new chunk at sentence i?
options: Similarity is above threshold and the current chunk is empty
Every sentence has a different token count
The adjacent-sentence similarity is below threshold and the current chunk is at least min_chars long
Only when the text contains a comma
questions.explanation: The split condition is sim < threshold and len(current chunk) >= min_chars; otherwise the sentence is appended.

questions.question: What does each entry from chunk_parent_child contain?
options: Only a child index with no parent text
One embedding and its cosine score against the query
A token label for every word in the original document
A child string, its parent_idx, and the full parent string
questions.explanation: The mapping appends a dictionary with child, parent_idx, and parent for every recursively split child.

questions.question: When does retrieve_recall return True?
options: At least one top-k chunk contains at least one gold substring, case-insensitively
Every chunk contains every gold substring
The query has more tokens than the chunk
The highest cosine score is exactly one
questions.explanation: It checks any gold substring against any of the top-k chunk texts after lowercasing.

questions.question: Why might a parent-child strategy help a RAG answer about a short clause?
options: It removes all document context to reduce the prompt to one word
A small child can retrieve precisely while its larger parent supplies surrounding context
It guarantees semantic embeddings are unnecessary for every query
It makes every chunk the same length regardless of document structure
questions.explanation: The mapping preserves a retrievable child and the broader parent text, allowing retrieval and context assembly to use different scales.
